Wording used: 'Prequalification and preapproval letters both specify how much the lender is willing to lend to you' and the letters 'are not guaranteed loan offers'; 'Lenders use the terms prequalification and preapproval differently'; 'getting preapproved earlier in the process can be a good way to spot potential issues with your credit in time to correct them.' The card does not say how long a letter lasts or whether credit is pulled, beyond what CFPB says. Bank: no earlier card on preapproval.
headline:
Prequalified Or Preapproved?
The Word Matters Less
turn_1: Echo, the CFPB says a prequalification or preapproval letter shows how much a lender is willing to lend you. It is not a guaranteed loan offer.
turn_2: So which one do I need? I thought preapproved was the real one.
turn_3: The CFPB says lenders use the two words differently. It also says getting preapproved earlier can help you spot credit issues in time to correct them.
echo_line: So the name on the letter matters less than I thought. I'd get mine early, before I fall for a house.
source: CFPB, prequalification and preapproval letters, consumerfinance.gov · retrieved Oct 17, 2026
